'''Usha N. Mallik''' (1947{{spnd}}4 August 2024) was an Indian-American experimental [[particle physicist]] and professor at the [[University of Iowa]].
She conducted studies of fundamental physics and developed detector readout software for [[particle collider]] experiments at [[SLAC]], [[DESY]], and [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Obituary of Usha Mallik {{!}} Physics and Astronomy - College of Liberal Arts and Sciences {{!}} The University of Iowa |url=https://physics.uiowa.edu/news/2024/08/obituary-usha-mallik |access-date=2026-09-07 |website=physics.uiowa.edu |language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==

Mallik was born in [[Calcutta, India]] in 1947. 
She studied under Sam J. Lindenbaum at the [[City College of New York]],
and obtained a PhD in physics in 1978.

As a postdoc, Mallik worked on particle collider experiments at [[DESY]] in Hamburg, Germany
and at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]] in California, USA.
At DESY,
Mallik studied [[electron–positron annihilation|electron–positron collisions]] in
the [[Positron-Electron Tandem Ring Accelerator|PETRA storage ring]]
and electron–proton collisions from the [[HERA (particle accelerator)|HERA storage ring]].
In part for her measurements of the [[J/Psi meson]] there, Mallik was recognized as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |access-date=2026-09-07 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

Mallik joined the University of Iowa as an assistant professor in 1989.
In the early 2000s, her group worked on the [[BaBar]] experiment at SLAC.
Starting in 2010, Mallik and her group began working on the [[ATLAS experiment]] at CERN's [[Large Hadron Collider]].
<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-02 |title=Meet 7 inspiring women from the ATLAS experiment |url=https://atlas.cern/updates/news/meet-7-inspiring-women-atlas-experiment |access-date=2026-09-07 |website=ATLAS |language=en}}</ref>
